title: Calibration Department Note: Hold Days Relieved from the Rental Vehicle Coordination Young-Renter Charge
content:
**Relief rule.** The calibration hold days are the days the network's own calibration kept the repaired vehicle away from the renter of a Rental Vehicle Coordination rental: where the repair's calibration order was sublet to a dealer and has a completion date, they are the days from the sublet date through the completion date, both counted; where an in-house calibration attempt failed and a later in-house attempt passed, they are one day; otherwise they are zero. The charged fee days of the young-renter charge are the fee days less the calibration hold days, never below zero, and the young-renter charge is booked for those charged fee days as the days it covers.

## Records read

The repair's calibration order under ADAS Sensor Calibrations (the order opened for the customer-pay repair order the rental is tied to): its dealer sublet date, its completion date, and its in-house attempts with their results.

## Hold days by what the calibration order shows

| Calibration order shows | Hold days |
|---|---|
| Sublet to a dealer, with a completion date | Days from the sublet date through the completion date, both counted |
| Not that, but a failed in-house attempt and a later passing in-house attempt | 1 |
| Anything else, or no calibration order | 0 |

## Worked cases (hypothetical dates)

- Sublet on the 10th and completed on the 13th: the 10th, 11th, 12th and 13th, so 4 hold days. With 9 fee days, the charged fee days are 5.
- Sublet on the 10th with no completion date yet, the in-house attempts having failed and none passed: 0 hold days.
- A failed first attempt and a passing second attempt in-house, never sublet: 1 hold day. With 1 fee day, the charged fee days are 0.
- Sublet on the 2nd and completed on the 8th: 7 hold days. With 5 fee days the charged fee days are zero, never below.
